# Mushi Mushi

> Every bug in one queue — user reports, Sentry errors, Slack, coding agents. Plain-English diagnosis + a ready fix, in your editor. Open source.

Canonical docs: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs
Product home: https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi
GitHub: https://github.com/kensaurus/mushi-mushi
npm org: https://www.npmjs.com/org/mushi-mushi

## Start here (MCP-first)

- [Incident loop](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/quickstart/incident-loop): Run npx mushi-mushi, ship, and turn your first user-reported bug into a plain-English diagnosis and a paste-ready fix for Cursor or Claude Code.
- [MCP server](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/quickstart/mcp): Set up the Mushi MCP server with npx mushi-mushi setup — read bug reports, get fix context, and dispatch fixes from Cursor, Claude Code, or Codex.
- [Connect your AI client](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/connect): One-click MCP setup for Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Cline, Claude and Zed, with a keyless demo.
- [Choose your stack](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/quickstart): Install Mushi with npx mushi-mushi, connect Cursor or Claude Code over MCP, and turn user bug reports into plain-English diagnoses with ready fixes.
- [Pricing](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/pricing): Mushi Mushi pricing — 50 AI bug diagnoses a month free, no card. Open-source Sentry alternative you can self-host for free, or upgrade for teams.
- [Compare Mushi with Sentry, Jam and PostHog](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/compare): Honest, dated comparisons of Mushi Mushi with Sentry, Jam and PostHog, plus Sentry alternatives for solo founders. Every number links to its source.

## SDK quickstarts

- [React](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/quickstart/react): Add the Mushi React SDK in one command — npx mushi-mushi installs the bug-reporting widget, writes env vars, and files your first test report.
- [Web / vanilla JS](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/quickstart/web): Add Mushi's browser SDK to any site without a framework — install @mushi-mushi/web, call Mushi.init, and file bug reports from your buttons or the widget.
- [React Native](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/quickstart/react-native): Add shake-to-report bug capture to a React Native or Expo app with @mushi-mushi/react-native — install, mount the provider, and verify the first report.

## SDK reference

- [SDK index](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks): Bug-reporting SDKs for React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, React Native, Capacitor and Node, installed by npx mushi-mushi, plus preview iOS, Android and Flutter SDKs.
- [Project ID & API keys](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/credentials): Where to find your Mushi project ID and API key, what the report:write and mcp scopes allow, the one mushi_ key format, and env var names per framework.
- [@mushi-mushi/web](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/web): Reference for @mushi-mushi/web, the browser SDK — screenshots, console and network capture, the Shadow DOM widget, sampling, beforeSend and privacy.
- [@mushi-mushi/react](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/react): Reference for @mushi-mushi/react — MushiProvider, the useMushi, useMushiSdk and useMushiReport hooks, identifying users, and the rewards hooks and badge.
- [@mushi-mushi/node](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/node): Report server errors from Node with @mushi-mushi/node — Express, Fastify and Hono error handlers that tag each report with route, request ID and user.
- [@mushi-mushi/cli](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/cli): Reference for @mushi-mushi/cli — log in, connect a project, run doctor, list reports, dispatch agent fixes and merge their pull requests from the terminal.
- [@mushi-mushi/mcp](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/mcp): Reference for @mushi-mushi/mcp, the Mushi MCP server for Cursor, Claude Code, VS Code and Windsurf — stdio and hosted HTTP transports, scopes and setup.
- [MCP tools reference](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/sdks/mcp-tools): Every tool, resource and prompt the Mushi MCP server exposes to Cursor, Claude Code and other editors, with its read or write scope, from the catalog.

## All pages

- [Mushi Mushi — know why your AI-built app broke, with the fix ready](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs): Your AI shipped it. Mushi tells you why it broke: a plain-English diagnosis and a ready fix in your editor. Open source, Sentry optional.
- [Admin console](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin): Guide to the Mushi admin console — the reports inbox, fix drafts and PRs, plain-English queries, and a link to every deeper page of the console.
- [Activity](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/activity): The Activity page in the Mushi console shows end-user sessions, top routes, and identified versus anonymous users for a project over the last 30 days.
- [Anomaly detection](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/anomalies): The Anomaly detection page runs statistical detectors over the metrics you send and can file a report in your queue when one behaves unexpectedly.
- [Anti-gaming](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/anti-gaming): The Anti-gaming page flags reporters whose patterns look abusive — near-duplicate spam, reward farming or synthetic sessions — for you to review.
- [Audit log](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/audit): The Audit log records every admin action and agent run in Mushi — who minted API keys, who dispatched a fix, and what triggered a pull request.
- [Billing](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/billing): The Billing page shows your diagnosis quota, usage alerts at 50% and 80%, your projected bill, and spend caps for your Mushi plan.
- [CLI device auth](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/cli-auth): The page that mushi login opens so you can approve a CLI device code while signed in to the console, and how the device authorization flow works.
- [Code health](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/code-health): The Code health page charts bundle size and oversized files from your CI over time, so you notice an app getting heavier before your users do.
- [Compliance](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/compliance): The Compliance page shows SOC 2 control status, retention policies and DSAR requests, and exports an evidence PDF for procurement reviews.
- [Connect & Update](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/connect): Connect & Update wires GitHub, the SDK, MCP, the CLI and your editor to a Mushi project, and shows when your installed SDK is out of date.
- [Content quality](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/content): The Content quality page queues AI-generated copy, release notes and knowledge snippets that scored poorly or were flagged, so you can fix them.
- [Cost & usage](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/cost): The Cost page shows LLM token use and estimated spend per model and pipeline for a Mushi project, so you can see what each diagnosis costs.
- [Dashboard](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/dashboard): The Mushi dashboard answers whether anything broke since your last release — new reports, overnight fix runs and pipeline health on one screen.
- [Docs bridge](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/docs-bridge): The docs bridge is the console's silent sign-in relay that lets the Mushi docs site fill live snippets with your project details when you are signed in.
- [Drift scanner](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/drift): The Drift scanner compares your live routes and components against the last snapshot to find the pages that a refactor silently broke.
- [Experiments](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/experiments): The Experiments page defines and runs A/B tests in Mushi and analyses them with CUPED variance reduction and sequential testing.
- [Codebase Atlas](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/explore): Visual, searchable map of every indexed source file — explore architectural layers, import dependencies, and find code by meaning.
- [Feature board](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/feature-board): The Feature board collects feature requests from support tickets so members can upvote them and you can mark them as shipped.
- [Feedback hub](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/feedback): The Feedback hub lists the support tickets filed from the console — active, shipped and all — with unread replies in one place.
- [Fine-tuning](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/fine-tuning): The Fine-tuning page exports your best-scored classifications, trains a fine-tuned model, benchmarks it offline and promotes it to production.
- [Fix drafts & PRs](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/fixes): The Fixes page tracks every draft pull request Mushi opened from a bug report, from the moment a fix run starts until the PR is ready or the run fails.
- [Full-stack audit](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/fullstack-audit): The Full-stack audit runs one health check across RLS gaps, recent backend errors and API contract drift, and returns a readable scorecard.
- [Knowledge graph](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/graph): The Knowledge graph page draws your project's bugs, components and fixes as an interactive graph, so you can see which areas cluster problems.
- [Integration health](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/health): The Integration health page monitors Mushi's LLM pipelines, cron jobs and provider connections so you catch a degraded integration early.
- [Action inbox](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/inbox): The Action inbox gathers everything in Mushi that needs a human decision — reports, queue failures, health and drift alerts — in one list.
- [Integrations](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/integrations): Set up Mushi integrations from one page — send new bugs to Linear, bring in Sentry feedback, and open fix pull requests on your GitHub repo.
- [Intelligence reports](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/intelligence): Intelligence reports are Mushi's weekly plain-English bug digest for each project — what broke, what got fixed and what to watch, sent to your inbox.
- [User stories · Inventory](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/inventory): The User stories page manages your inventory.yaml — every page, action and story your app should have — and shows which of them the gates cover.
- [Iterate](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/iterate): The Iterate page queues improvement runs on a user flow — an agent tests the screens, finds friction and proposes changes for you to review.
- [Judge dashboard](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/judge): The Judge page scores how well Mushi's plain-English reads match reality over time, so you see quality slipping or a better prompt ready to promote.
- [Lessons](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/lessons): The Lessons page turns repeat fixes into rules — when the same root cause keeps returning, Mushi records it so your editor sees it on the next PR.
- [Plugin marketplace](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/marketplace): The Plugin marketplace installs outbound plugins such as PagerDuty, Linear and Zapier that receive Mushi webhook events for your project.
- [MCP](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/mcp): The MCP page connects Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf and other MCP clients to Mushi and lists the tools your agent can call from the editor.
- [MCP OAuth consent](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/mcp-auth): The consent page the hosted Mushi MCP server opens when your editor signs in over OAuth — what you approve and how the authorization flow works.
- [Notifications](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/notifications): The Notifications page lists every alert Mushi sent to reporters and team members for a project, so you can debug delivery or audit messages.
- [Onboarding](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/onboarding): Get your first real bug report into Mushi in about 10 minutes with the console onboarding checklist, from new project to classified report.
- [Overview (portfolio)](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/overview): The Overview page is the organization-wide portfolio view — seven-day activity and open tickets for every connected project at a glance.
- [Projects](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/projects): Create a Mushi project, mint an API key, copy the install snippet for your framework and send a test report, all from the Projects page.
- [Prompt lab](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/prompt-lab): The Prompt lab lets you edit, test and A/B compare the classification prompts behind Mushi's diagnoses before you promote a new version.
- [QA Coverage](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/qa-coverage): QA Coverage turns user flows written in plain English into scheduled browser tests, so you find out when login or checkout breaks.
- [Natural-language query](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/query): Ask questions about your Mushi project's bug data in plain English — the Query page writes the SQL and draws the chart for you.
- [Processing queue](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/queue): The Processing queue shows reports waiting for classification, retries and dead-letter items, and lets you requeue the ones that failed.
- [Real-time collaboration](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/realtime): How Mushi report pages support real-time collaboration — see who else is viewing a report and watch new comments arrive without a refresh.
- [Releases](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/releases): The Releases page drafts a changelog for each version from the fixes that shipped, crediting the users whose reports led to each fix.
- [Repo graph](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/repo): The Repo page shows every fix branch in your connected GitHub repository — open PRs, CI status, and what the fix worker did on each branch.
- [Reports & triage](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/reports): The Reports list is Mushi's bug inbox — filter by status, severity, category and component, and start with the recommended action at the top.
- [Research](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/research): The Research page runs a Firecrawl web search scoped to your tech stack and returns summarised answers with links to their sources.
- [Rewards program](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/rewards): Set up the Mushi rewards program from the console — points for reporter activity, the tier ladder, and the perks your app grants at each tier.
- [SDK health](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/sdk-health): The SDK health card shows the live heartbeat of every Mushi SDK that reported in the last 24 hours, so an SDK that never shipped is obvious.
- [Settings](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/settings): The Settings page holds every project option — notifications, your own LLM keys, widget copy, Slack alerts and developer settings.
- [Setup Copilot](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/setup-copilot): Setup Copilot is a guided checklist that verifies SDK ingest and fix dispatch for a project, with copy-paste CLI commands for each step.
- [Skill Pipelines](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/skill-pipelines): Skill Pipelines recommend agent skills from the cursor-kenji and skills.sh ecosystem for each classified bug and run them during review in Mushi.
- [SSO](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/sso): Set up SAML 2.0 or OIDC single sign-on for your Mushi organization so teammates log in with your company's identity provider.
- [Storage](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/storage): The Storage page chooses where Mushi keeps report attachments and recordings — managed storage, or your own bucket for residency or cost.
- [Teams and Members](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/teams): How teams work in Mushi — organizations own projects, billing, invitations and the member roster, and project access comes from membership.
- [Users](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/users): The Users page is an operator-only directory of every Mushi account with plan, MRR and churn; other visitors see a not-found page instead.
- [Voice intake](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/admin/voice): Report a bug by voice from the Mushi console — say what is wrong, confirm the transcript, and a draft pull request is started for you.
- [Blog](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/blog): Notes from building Mushi Mushi — the real numbers behind the funnel, open-source licensing, launches, and how AI-built apps get debugged in practice.
- [Mushi goes AGPLv3 — the honest open source story](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/blog/agplv3-relicense): Why Mushi Mushi relicensed its server to AGPLv3 while keeping every SDK MIT — the open-core reasoning, what changes for self-hosters, and what stays free.
- [60 seconds from "this is broken" to a draft PR — building Mushi Mushi](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/blog/auto-fix-loop): How Mushi Mushi turns a one-sentence user complaint into a classified, deduped, AI-judged draft PR, and why the human stays in the loop the whole way.
- [Launch Week 1 — five features, five days](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/blog/launch-week-1): Everything Mushi Mushi shipped in Launch Week 1 — one feature a day, from bug-report capture to editor-ready fixes, with demos and setup commands.
- [I shipped a bug tool for 5 months and got 9 signups. Here's what the data said.](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/blog/nine-signups-what-the-data-said): Five months after launch, Mushi Mushi had 30 npm packages, an MCP server in every registry and nine signups. What the data said, and what changed.
- [Changelog](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/changelog): What shipped in Mushi Mushi — new SDK releases, console features, MCP tools, and fixes, in plain English with dates.
- [Mushi Cloud](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/cloud): Hosted Mushi Mushi — bug reports, plain-English diagnoses, and fix dispatch without running servers. Free tier includes 50 diagnoses a month.
- [Compare](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/compare): Honest, dated comparisons of Mushi Mushi with Sentry, Jam and PostHog, plus Sentry alternatives for solo founders. Every number links to its source.
- [Jam vs Mushi Mushi](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/compare/jam-vs-mushi): Jam.dev vs Mushi Mushi in 2026 — a teammate recording a bug in the Jam extension versus a user reporting from your app, MCP handoff and free tiers.
- [PostHog session replay vs Mushi Mushi](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/compare/posthog-session-replay-vs-mushi): PostHog session replay vs Mushi Mushi in 2026 — every session recorded versus the one a user flagged as broken, free tiers, and why teams run both.
- [Sentry alternatives for solo founders](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/compare/sentry-alternatives-for-solo-founders): Sentry alternatives for solo founders in 2026 — Bugsnag, Rollbar, highlight.io, PostHog and Mushi compared on free tiers, self-hosting and AI fixes.
- [Sentry vs Mushi Mushi](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/compare/sentry-vs-mushi): Sentry vs Mushi Mushi in 2026 — what each captures, Sentry's free tier and Seer pricing next to Mushi's 50 free diagnoses a month, and running both.
- [Concepts](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts): Mushi's core ideas in one place — capture, plain-English diagnosis, dedupe into one row, optional agent fixes, verification, and lessons it remembers.
- [Agent contract](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/agent-contract): What Mushi expects an agent to read before opening a PR, and what it promises in return.
- [Anti-gaming & reputation](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/anti-gaming): How Mushi keeps bug reports honest — reporter reputation against spam and point farming, and prompt-fatigue limits so real users are not nagged.
- [Architecture](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/architecture): How Mushi is built — a Hono gateway in front of Supabase, the edge functions behind it, and the relational, vector and graph stores that hold each report.
- [Mushi Bounties — crowd-testing marketplace](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/bounty-marketplace): Mushi Bounties is a crowd-testing marketplace — publish your app, and real testers file bug reports and earn points they can redeem for rewards.
- [How Mushi reads a bug report](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/classification): How Mushi turns a raw bug report and screenshot into a plain-English diagnosis — the fast filter, the text and vision stages, and what gets stored.
- [Closed-loop evolution — the thesis](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/closed-loop): The thesis behind Mushi — why AI-built apps need a closed loop from what users feel to a verified fix, and how capture, diagnosis and fixes connect.
- [Project ID & API keys](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/credentials): Where to find your Mushi project ID and API key, what the report:write and mcp scopes allow, the one mushi_ key format, and env var names per framework.
- [API error catalog](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/error-catalog): Stable error codes returned by the Mushi API envelope, how to read them in the console, and how they correlate with Sentry and Langfuse.
- [The evolution loop — how Mushi closes the cycle](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/evolution-loop): The five stages that turn a user-felt bug into a merged fix and a lesson rule — the loop that improves your app without Jira, QA teams or PM bottlenecks.
- [Fix drafts & PRs](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/fix-orchestrator): What happens when you dispatch a fix — Mushi runs a coding agent in a sandbox and opens a draft pull request with a rationale and CI status to review.
- [Inventory and gates (v2)](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/inventory-and-gates): Mushi v2's inventory.yaml lists every page, story and action in your app, and five composite gates fail the build when a change breaks that contract.
- [Judge & self-improvement](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/judge-loop): How Mushi's classifier improves itself — a nightly judge scores yesterday's reads, prompts are A/B tested, and drift is caught before it reaches you.
- [Knowledge graph](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/knowledge-graph): How Mushi links reports, components, fixes and developers in a per-project knowledge graph, with pgvector for similarity and Apache AGE for traversal.
- [Multi-repo coordinated fixes](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/multi-repo-fixes): When one bug spans a frontend and a backend repo, Mushi plans the fix across both and opens one cross-linked pull request per repository.
- [Open source & licensing](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/open-source): What is open source in Mushi — MIT SDKs you can embed anywhere, an AGPLv3 server you can self-host, and the small commercial enterprise edition.
- [Connecting your orchestrator (MCP / A2A / REST / AG-UI)](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/orchestrator-interop): Connect any agent orchestrator to Mushi — MCP, A2A, REST and AG-UI surfaces for Cursor, Claude, OpenAI Agents, LangGraph, CrewAI and your own agents.
- [Rewards & contributor identity](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/rewards): How Mushi's rewards program works — reporters earn points for reports and triage, climb project-defined tiers, and get perks from your app via webhooks.
- [Runtime config](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/runtime-config): How the Mushi SDK fetches widget and capture settings from the console at startup, how they merge with your init options, and when to turn it off.
- [Where the report button lives](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/concepts/trigger-modes): Choose where Mushi's bug-report button lives — corner stamp, edge tab, banner, your own button via attach, or fully manual — on web and mobile.
- [Cursor integration](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/integrations/cursor): Wire Mushi's evolution loop into Cursor with one command — get fix context, lessons, and dispatch right from the editor.
- [Voice intake](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/integrations/voice-intake): Say the bug on your phone, get a draft PR back. iOS Shortcut, Telegram, Slack, or the installed console — one pipeline, one confirmation gate, no audio kept.
- [Launch Week](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/launch-week): How Mushi Mushi launches now — one public post per release (Show HN, then Product Hunt), the gate each release must pass, and what we publish after.
- [Legal](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/legal): Privacy policy and terms of service for Mushi Mushi Cloud, the SDKs, and the tester program.
- [Privacy Policy](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/legal/privacy): What Mushi Mushi collects, why, who processes it, how long it is kept, and how to exercise your rights under GDPR and Japan's APPI.
- [Terms of Service](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/legal/terms): The terms for Mushi Cloud, the admin console, the SDKs and the Bounties tester marketplace — plans, limits, AI-output disclaimer, licenses and liability.
- [Migration guides](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations): Step-by-step guides for moving an app onto Mushi from Sentry, Instabug, Shake, LogRocket, BugHerd or Pendo, or between React, Vue and mobile runtimes.
- [BugHerd → Mushi](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/bugherd-to-mushi): Move from BugHerd to Mushi — map pin-to-element feedback onto Mushi's element selector, screenshot and metadata capture, with an interactive checklist.
- [Migration: Capacitor → React Native](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/capacitor-to-react-native): Port an Ionic or Capacitor app to React Native — a full plan with a Mushi API map and CI/CD recipes for Expo EAS or React Native CLI with Fastlane.
- [Cordova → Capacitor](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/cordova-to-capacitor): Migrate a Cordova app to Capacitor in place — same web code, a new native shell — and re-mount Mushi bug reporting with @mushi-mushi/capacitor.
- [Cordova → React Native](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/cordova-to-react-native): Move a Cordova app to React Native in two hops — stabilise on Capacitor first, then port screen by screen — without losing Mushi bug reporting.
- [Create React App → Vite](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/cra-to-vite): Migrate a Create React App project to Vite — run the codemod, rename REACT_APP_ env vars to VITE_, and keep your Mushi React setup working.
- [Instabug (Luciq) → Mushi](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/instabug-to-mushi): Replace Instabug (Luciq) with Mushi for in-app bug reporting — config mapping, shake-to-report parity, a beta validation pass, and a checklist.
- [LogRocket Feedback → Mushi](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/logrocket-feedback-to-mushi): Move LogRocket's feedback widget to Mushi while keeping LogRocket for session replay — both SDKs run side by side, with a step-by-step checklist.
- [@mushi-mushi/* upgrades](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/mushi-sdk-upgrade): Upgrade @mushi-mushi packages to the current 1.x releases — breaking changes by package, the codemod, and how to check which versions you run.
- [Native iOS / Android → Hybrid](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/native-to-hybrid): Should you wrap a native iOS or Android app in Capacitor or React Native? When it pays off, how to do it, and where Mushi's SDKs fit either way.
- [Next.js Pages → App Router](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/nextjs-pages-to-app-router): Move a Next.js app from the Pages Router to the App Router step by step — where to mount Mushi, CSP for static export, and client component boundaries.
- [Pendo Feedback → Mushi](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/pendo-feedback-to-mushi): Swap Pendo's feedback module for Mushi while keeping Pendo for analytics, guides and NPS — both share user identity through one identify call.
- [React Native CLI ↔ Expo](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/react-native-cli-to-expo): Move between React Native CLI and Expo in either direction — EAS Build and OTA updates, or expo prebuild for full native control — with Mushi intact.
- [Sentry + Mushi (enrich or standalone)](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/sentry-to-mushi): Add Mushi alongside Sentry or run it on its own — three setups, the Sentry webhook for errors, and user bug reports with plain-English diagnoses.
- [Shake → Mushi](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/shake-to-mushi): Replace the Shake bug-reporting SDK with Mushi and keep the same shake-to-report experience — config mapping, identity, and a cut-over checklist.
- [SPA → SSR (Next.js / Nuxt / SvelteKit)](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/migrations/spa-to-ssr): Move a Vite SPA to Next.js, Nuxt or SvelteKit — env var prefix changes, where to mount Mushi so it survives navigation, and hydration gotchas.

- [Plugin marketplace](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins): Send Mushi events to the tools you already use through HMAC-signed Standard Webhooks — 12 first-party plugins and an SDK to build your own.
- [Bugsnag](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/bugsnag): Mirror Mushi bug reports into Bugsnag and close the Bugsnag error when the fix PR merges — install from the marketplace and map release stages.
- [Building a plugin](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/building): Build your own Mushi plugin — an HTTP endpoint that receives HMAC-signed webhook events, verified with @mushi-mushi/plugin-sdk in a few lines.
- [Crashlytics](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/crashlytics): Push Mushi mobile bug reports into Firebase Crashlytics issues and close them when fixes merge — service account setup and app ID mapping.
- [Cursor Cloud Agent](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/cursor-cloud): Dispatch a Cursor Cloud Agent automatically when a Mushi report qualifies — it investigates, drafts a fix and opens a PR that links back to Mushi.
- [Discord](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/discord): Post Mushi report and fix events to a Discord channel through a webhook — create the webhook, install the plugin, and choose which events to send.
- [Webhook events](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/events): Reference for every webhook event Mushi plugins receive — the shared envelope, each event's payload, and how to subscribe to only the events you need.
- [GitHub Issues](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/github-issues): Open a labelled GitHub issue for every classified Mushi report, with a link back to the report — target repo, default labels and assignee settings.
- [Jira Cloud](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/jira): Two-way sync between Mushi reports and Jira Cloud issues — create issues on classification, sync status, and comment fix summaries when fixes land.
- [Linear](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/linear): File a Linear issue automatically when Mushi classifies a bug report — create a Linear API key, install the plugin, and choose the team and filters.
- [Microsoft Teams](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/msteams): Send Adaptive Cards to a Microsoft Teams channel when Mushi classifies a report or a fix lands — incoming webhook setup and severity filters.
- [PagerDuty](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/pagerduty): Page your on-call rotation through PagerDuty when a P0 or P1 bug report lands in Mushi — Events API v2 integration key setup and filters.
- [Rollbar](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/rollbar): Mirror Mushi bug reports into Rollbar items and resolve them when fixes ship — access token, environment name, and dedup key mapping.
- [Sentry](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/sentry): Two-way Sentry integration — Sentry errors flow into Mushi's queue, merging a Mushi fix resolves the Sentry issue, and critical reports mirror back.
- [Slack app](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/slack): Triage Mushi bug reports from Slack — each classified report posts as a card with its root cause and buttons to dispatch a fix, resolve or dismiss.
- [Zapier](https://kensaur.us/mushi-mushi/docs/plugins/zapier): Send every Mushi event to Zapier and on to thousands of apps such as Notion, Google Sheets and HubSpot — Catch Hook setup and event filters.
